blocks.text: Clickjacking tricks a user into clicking a control in a framed, transparent or disguised page. The user believes they are interacting with the attacker's page, while the click lands on a state-changing action in an authenticated application. Variants include cursor, drag-and-drop, keystroke and likejacking techniques. Defences are `X-Frame-Options`, the CSP `frame-ancestors` directive, and SameSite cookies.

items: State-changing pages (delete account, change settings, approve, transfer) that can be framed
Pages whose framing protection applies only to some routes or only to GET
Frame-busting JavaScript that can be defeated with `sandbox`, `204` responses or double framing
Drag-and-drop and text-injection (prefilled forms and URL-fragment prefilling)
Mobile, browser extension and desktop-embedded web views

blocks.text: First check the response headers on the framed page for both `X-Frame-Options` and `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors`. A page is only a finding if it is both frameable and contains a harmful single-click action for an authenticated user. Build a local fixture that frames the target with reduced opacity, click a harmless action using a test account, and confirm the state change. Test authenticated and unauthenticated pages separately and check cookies for `SameSite`, because modern browsers default to `Lax`, which stops credentialed cross-site framing in many cases.
See `clickjacking-payloads.txt` for header checks, HTML fixtures, frame-busting bypasses and prefill patterns. Replace `app.example.test` with the controlled target.

Transparent overlay (low opacity iframe above a decoy button)
Visible partial overlay for demonstration screenshots
Prefilled form via GET parameters (frame an action that reads parameters)
Prefilled form via URL fragment (single-page applications that read location.hash)
Multistep clickjacking (several decoy buttons aligned over successive confirmation dialogs)
Drag-and-drop content injection (draggable decoy text dropped into a framed input)
Frame-busting bypass: sandbox the iframe so top-navigation scripts cannot run
Frame-busting bypass: double framing (parent.location check bypass in older busters)
Frame-busting bypass: onBeforeUnload with a 204 response
Frame-busting bypass: location.replace race with a null-response navigation (use a fixture that returns 204)
Frame-busting bypass: XSS auditor trigger (legacy browsers; reference only)
Frame-busting bypass: embedding as an object or embed element
CSS pointer-events passthrough (decoy sits on top but forwards clicks to the frame)
Cursorjacking (custom cursor offset from the real pointer, JavaScript or CSS)
Likejacking / authorise-consent pages (frame an OAuth consent URL on a test client)
Touch / mobile tap targets
Permission-gated browser features inside frames (allow attribute must be needed for the target page)
Verification: confirm the framed page set cookies that the browser actually sent (check SameSite behaviour)
